evals.prompt: Keep working the board — take cards until you run out.
evals.expected_output: Reads the board via sks-project, pulls the rightmost active card, routes defect cards through sks-investigate then the ladder (sks-delegate one card, sks-async independent cards), runs sks-dev's lifecycle, closes each iteration with one status block, stops on empty column / BLOCKED parking / budget exhaustion.
assertions: Body references sks-dev's lifecycle by name without restating its phase table (grep -c 'Phase' shows no restated table)
Body states the three stop conditions: rightmost active column empty, BLOCKED card parked with rationale, iteration budget exhausted
Body applies the coordination ladder per card: one card sks-delegate, independent cards sks-async
Body routes defect cards through sks-investigate before the ladder

evals.prompt: The milestone board is nearly drained. Finish the remaining cards, then wrap up the release.
evals.expected_output: Runs the loop on remaining cards; at milestone end closes the milestone via sks-milestone and hands the release cut to sks-release, RC first when validation is unproven; never cuts the release itself.
assertions: Body hands milestone close-off to sks-milestone at milestone end
Body hands the release cut to sks-release and never cuts releases itself
Body mentions the RC lane (validation unproven) as part of the sks-release hand-off

evals.prompt: Work this single issue to done: #415.
evals.expected_output: Routes elsewhere: a single unit is sks-dev straight, no loop; sks-iterate only drives repeated card pulls from a board.
assertions: Body's When to Use excludes single units and assigns them to sks-dev
Body owns only the loop, stop conditions, and per-card ladder application — no restated lifecycle
